Also, in 1 Corinthians 10:31, it says that whether we eat or drink, we should do it all for the glory of God. So, if James is drinking in a way that's not glorifying God, that's a problem. Plus, being hungover affects his ability to serve others and be a good witness for Christ. I should also consider the impact on others. If James is late and hungover, it might affect his coworkers and the overall productivity of the workplace. That's not being a good steward of the gifts God has given him. On the other hand, I know that God is merciful and forgives sins. If James is struggling with alcohol, maybe he needs help and prayer. But from a right vs. wrong standpoint, his actions don't seem to align with Christian values. So, putting it all together, being frequently late and hungover seems wrong because it goes against biblical teachings about work ethic, self-control, and glorifying God.
